hard: Establish exactly one repository-owned execution-profile policy authority for the managed Codex and Antigravity defaults. Adapter-owned duplicated default model/effort policy is forbidden. The policy must preserve gpt-5.6-sol/high for Codex and gemini-3.8-flash/high for Antigravity throughout TASK-162.

Model identifiers are opaque provider-native identifiers subject only to bounded deterministic syntax/size validation. Do not introduce a repository- global model allowlist. A syntactically valid synthetic future model identifier must be able to flow through profile validation and exact native command construction without adding that identifier to source code.

Reasoning/effort capability validation must be deterministic and repository-owned for each managed Executor. Invalid effort values must fail before native invocation. Capability validation must not score, rank, choose, downgrade, or substitute a model or effort.

A resolved execution profile must bind at minimum exact run_id, executor, model, reasoning_effort, and deterministic source attribution for model and effort. The profile must be immutable once bound to one admitted native execution authorization.

For canonical Operator paths using Codex or Antigravity, resolve/validate the profile before native invocation, persist an immutable profile sidecar only after exact RUN identity exists, and guarantee that the sidecar is durably present before the native runner is entered. Failure to validate or persist the profile must invoke zero native Executors.

Re-persisting an identical bound profile for the same RUN may be idempotent; conflicting executor/model/effort/source content for an existing RUN profile must fail closed before invocation. A later repository default change must never alter an already-bound RUN profile.

Dispatcher selection remains exactly-one and executor-neutral. For managed Executors it must require consistency among selected Executor, RUN.executor, and profile.executor, then inject the exact bound profile into the native adapter. It must not inspect TASK difficulty, cost, benchmark history, or choose another profile.

Codex and Antigravity PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR command construction must consume the same exact bound profile values. Preserve all existing schema-output, timeout, sandbox/mutation, direct-execution instruction, structural ResultPackage, and no-retry/no-fallback semantics.

Direct repository smoke utilities may be adjusted only as needed to consume the single repository-owned default policy rather than relying on adapter- owned defaults. They must remain isolated utility surfaces and must not become a second profile authority or canonical TASK-162 network verification path.

Profile provenance must survive both RESULT and FAILURE terminal transport as a separate immutable execution-profile artifact associated with the exact RUN. Existing transport idempotency/conflict checks must include the profile when one is expected. Historical terminal artifacts without a profile remain valid and must not be reinterpreted or rejected.

Do not fabricate an execution profile for pre-RUN admission failures, direct-candidate acceptance, reusable-package paths, verification-only recovery, or any flow that does not actually authorize a new managed native Executor invocation. If a native invocation begins and later fails, its exact persisted profile provenance must remain available.

Future compatible default-model evolution is a required architectural invariant: when an already-supported Executor keeps the same native model/ effort invocation contract, changing its default model must require only repository-owned profile-policy change plus focused validation/smoke, not adapter, Dispatcher, frozen RUN, carrier, or lifecycle redesign.
Do not modify files outside scope.modify and do not push or publish from Executor implementation.

task.problem: TASK-061 made native model selection deterministic by hard-coding gpt-5.6-sol/high in the Codex adapter and gemini-3.8-flash/high in the Antigravity adapter. That solved ambient-machine drift but made adapters own default-selection policy, left canonical RUN identity unable to attribute the exact native model/effort actually requested, and would force repeated source redesign as compatible model generations evolve. The Human has now authorized the execution-profile-selection-v1 side-track: TASK-162 must build the deterministic profile/provenance foundation without yet exposing Human per-execution overrides or activating the new GPT-6 Sol Medium / Gemini 3.8 Flash Medium defaults. Exact profile provenance must survive terminal transport, not exist only on one self-host filesystem, while frozen TASK/RUN semantics and all execution, verification, review, and publication authorities remain intact.
